title: The sideways step needs its own condition
question: Why do the transverse coordinates stay unchanged?
recap: The longitudinal light constraints do not alone determine transverse scale. Enforcing the isotropic light-speed condition on transverse propagation, together with the inverse and positive identity limit, completes the map.
premises: Use the scale fixed in the longitudinal transformation.
Light has the same speed in all spatial directions, not only along x.
limitations: Checking a single axial ray cannot test transverse normalization.
Matrix determinants and interval checks verify this result but do not replace its stated physical premises.

overview.text: The longitudinal light constraints do not alone determine transverse scale. Enforcing the isotropic light-speed condition on transverse propagation, together with the inverse and positive identity limit, completes the map.

full.text: Write \(y' = b(v)\,y\) for a transverse axis. On a ray with \(x = 0\), \(y = ct\), the already determined longitudinal map gives \(x' = -\gamma v t\) and \(t' = \gamma t\). Requiring the transformed ray’s speed to be \(c\) gives \(\gamma^2 v^2 + b^2 c^2 = \gamma^2 c^2\), hence \(b^2 = 1\).
The positive, identity-connected choice gives \(y' = y\) and likewise \(z' = z\). The inverse map replaces \(v\) with \(-v\) and exchanges primed and unprimed quantities.

full.spoken: The inverse transformation uses plus v and exchanges the two frames.

full.text: At \(v = 0.6c\), \(\gamma = 1.25\). In units where \(c = 1\), the event \((t, x) = (2, 1)\) becomes \((1.75, -0.25)\); the inverse returns \((2, 1)\). The coordinate-map laboratory can check the same map from either direction.

full.returnCaption: Return to why do the transverse coordinates stay unchanged.

items: Introduce an independent transverse scale rather than assuming it is one.
Transform a ray originally perpendicular to the boost.
Require the full transformed speed, including its longitudinal component, to equal c.
Solve for the transverse scale and select the positive identity-connected branch.
Apply the inverse to a complete event, not just its spatial coordinate.

margin.text: Modern verification may check \(c^2t^2 - x^2 - y^2 - z^2\) or the matrix determinant. Those checks are labeled as consequences of this map, not imported as the historical derivation’s starting point.
